newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU raises export taxes on wheat, to reject bids.
newsitem.headline: EU raises export taxes on wheat, to reject bids.

text.p: The European Union on Tuesday hiked export taxes for soft wheat and durum and was poised to reject about 800,000 tonnes of bids to export soft wheat at a previous tax of 0.5 Ecus a tonne, member country officials said.

The EU's executive Commission raised the fixed tax which applies to its daily grain export channel to three Ecus per tonne from 0.5 Ecus for soft wheat, the officials said. It also doubled the durum export tax to 10 Ecus and raised a tax on soft wheat flour exports to four Ecus from 0.7 Ecus per tonne.

The effect of the move is to tighten an export channel which had been left ajar for some commercial business, but which had sparked a sudden rush of bids as world wheat prices converged and the soaring dollar made European wheat more competitive.
Officials said the Commission had signalled it would reject bids for at least 830,000 tonnes of wheat made since Friday.
"It looks like a refusal," said a French grain official, adding this had not been officially confirmed.

While the European Commission was willing to cover short-term business at a modest tax, it was less willing to shore up potentially major long positions for later this year when French wheat was at a discount, European grain sources said. Licences issued in August are valid until end-December.
